checkpoints.description: [1/2] Make ui abort recover from a corrupt record and refuse a vanished surface with a triad

impact_assessment.why: read_task names 'run ui abort' as the remedy for a corrupt record, but abort called read_task too, so the remedy raised the same error - a dead end. Measured with a valid contract and a corrupt ui_task.json: both read_task and abort raised 'The UI task record is unreadable'. Separately, abort did contract.surfaces[str(task['surface'])]; a surface removed from the contract raised a bare KeyError('app') instead of a Why/Fix triad.
impact_assessment.benefits: The remedy the guard prints now works: abort drops an unreadable record (keeping its bytes) and says nothing could be restored. A vanished surface produces a readable triad naming the surface and the file to delete, instead of a stack trace.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: abort's result gains dropped_corrupt_record only on the corrupt path; a missing record still raises 'No UI task is open'; the stale-but-valid record is kept; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: ui_contract.py, aikit_cli.py, three tests
impact_assessment.mitigation: corrupt path returns before any git call; a missing record still raises because the file check distinguishes them; each new test fails first with the exact error

checkpoints.description: [2/2] abort drops a corrupt record (bytes preserved) and names a vanished surface in a triad; CLI prints the drop; 3 fail-first tests; 1044 unit + 89 integration green; budget 9.87ms/405ms

[1/2] Replace the archive 'unarchive it first' remedy, which names a command that does not exist

impact_assessment.why: archive_project's already-archived triad told the operator to 'unarchive it first', but AIKit has no unarchive command (confirmed against `aikit.py --help`: archive exists, unarchive does not). The remedy was unactionable. Archiving sets archived/archived_at/archive_reason in .aikit/project.json, moves the folder and rewrites the README, so revival is manual by design.
impact_assessment.benefits: The failure now names a real action (clear the archived flag in .aikit/project.json) instead of a command the operator cannot run, matching the honest 'no reverse transition' entry in the state-machine doc.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: message text only, exit code stays 1; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: project_archive.py, one test
impact_assessment.mitigation: one string change; the test asserts the fix names project.json and not the phantom command, and the existing unarchived-JSON test still passes

[1/2] status --json reports the seven project-level machine states it can read, and names the fourteen it did not sample

impact_assessment.why: P11 asked to complete status --json with every machine's state. Only 4 of 21 were visible before (license tier, disruption, ui_task_open, gate names) and a bare status string could not be resolved to a machine. Reading the other 14 would mean Reforge runs, the Idea Catcher register, delegation transcripts, upstream checks, compat proofs and proof artifacts - work a cold-start status call must not do.
impact_assessment.benefits: An agent holding a status string from a project's own state can now see which machine it belongs to and what the live value is, and the payload states its own coverage instead of implying a full snapshot, so nobody mistakes 7 of 21 for all 21.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: adds a machines key to the status --json payload, existing keys unchanged; dependency: one new module importing existing readers; concurrency: none; state: a new module, aikit_cli, tests, two docs
impact_assessment.mitigation: each reported state is asserted to be a declared state of its machine; read_count plus not_sampled is asserted to equal the registry exactly; a reader failure becomes a named error, never a traceback or a state outside the vocabulary; --help import graph verified to pull none of the new code

[1/2] Refuse publish on an archived project (P6, publish half only)

impact_assessment.why: The state-machine inventory's Project row recorded 'publish/check never refuse an archived project'. Verified live: cmd_publish never called is_archived, so `publish` on an archived project ran the whole pipeline and reached a later gate (measured exit 1) instead of refusing. Archiving retires the project, moves it to projects/archive/ and archives the GitHub repository, so publishing one presents a retired project as live.
impact_assessment.benefits: A retired project can no longer be re-published by mistake, and the refusal names the real recovery path (move it out of projects/archive/ and clear the flag), consistent with ADR-400's archive remedy.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: publish gains a refusal, exit 2, before any disk change; check is deliberately unchanged because a read-only audit of an archived project may be legitimate; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: aikit_cli.py, one test
impact_assessment.mitigation: the guard runs before the pre-push hook is installed, so a refused publish writes nothing; the full TestProjectRegistry class (123 tests) was run to prove no existing publish path regressed

[1/2] Publish the status vocabulary in top-level help as a pointer to the registry, not a copy

impact_assessment.why: P12 proposed copying each machine's states into every --help. Measured first: argparse already publishes ui-id's kinds and archive's flags via choices=, and idea_catcher publishes its statuses, so the premise was largely already delivered. What remained genuinely missing was discoverability of the seven derived vocabularies in status --json, which no --help names. Copying 88 state names into a generated, pinned help string would create a second source of truth for them, the exact drift this audit keeps fixing.
impact_assessment.benefits: One line in --help tells an agent where every vocabulary lives and how to resolve a bare status, without duplicating any of it; the pin also fails if a future change copies a machine's states into the help.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: top-level help text gains an epilog, so aikit_help.py must be regenerated or the ADR-180 pin fails; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: aikit_parser.py, aikit_help.py, one test
impact_assessment.mitigation: the generated string was rebuilt from the grammar rather than hand-edited, so the pin still proves the fast path matches; the new test asserts the pointer exists and that no machine's states appear verbatim

[1/2] Enforce the idea-status machine on the write path (P5), leaving existing history untouched

impact_assessment.why: The inventory recorded that validate_ideas has no transition table, so a hand-edited register can reopen a terminal row; only Blocked and Superseded were guarded in _apply_status. Measured the blast radius from each idea's own history: 641 real transitions across 1751 ideas, of which exactly 6 violate the documented machine (4x Rejected->Deferred, 1x Superseded->Deferred, 1x Rejected->Integrated). Those 6 are historical rows, so a retroactive validate check would fail the live register for history that cannot be rewritten.
impact_assessment.benefits: A forbidden move through set-status is now refused with the legal targets named, so the register cannot be pushed into a state its own machine does not allow; legal edges are unaffected.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: set-status gains a refusal (exit 1) for moves outside the table; idea_catcher must not import scripts, so the table is declared locally and pinned by a test; existing history is untouched; dependency: none; concurrency: the register write path is unchanged; state: registry.py, 2 tests
impact_assessment.mitigation: the local table was verified byte-identical to the registry before wiring; a test pins them so they cannot drift; all 39 idea_catcher tests pass; the live register still validates, renders and reports exactly the same 133 pre-existing aegean-tge problems and zero aikit ones
